title: A Pact above the Kettle
story: The flatmates argued about the kettle, the shower, and a phone alarm that rang three times. Finally they made a simple pact. Rafi would shower first, and Leah would use the kitchen first, so neither would wait in the hall. Alarms would live in bedrooms, not in the shared room. For four days it worked. On Friday Rafi forgot and set the loud alarm beside the sofa. Leah left it there and went to make tea, which made him more ashamed than a complaint would have. He moved the phone and wrote the pact above the kettle. The next week was not perfect, but the mornings were calmer.

vocabulary.definition: An agreement about how people will act.
A phone signal meant to wake someone.
Sorry and uncomfortable about something you did.
A criticism spoken when something displeases you.

quiz.question: What morning order did the pact set?
options: Rafi would shower first, and Leah would use the kitchen first
Leah would shower first, and Rafi would cook first
Both of them would use the kitchen at the same moment
The alarms would stay in the shared room
quiz.correctAnswer: Rafi would shower first, and Leah would use the kitchen first
quiz.explanation: The pact said Rafi would shower first and Leah would use the kitchen first.
quiz.supportingSentence: Rafi would shower first, and Leah would use the kitchen first, so neither would wait in the hall.

quiz.question: What does writing the pact above the kettle suggest?
options: Rafi wanted the agreement in a place they would see every morning
He had decided to throw the kettle away
He was moving out of the flat that night
He wanted Leah to stop using the kitchen
quiz.correctAnswer: Rafi wanted the agreement in a place they would see every morning
quiz.explanation: He writes the pact above the kettle, a spot used in the morning routine, so it will stay visible.
quiz.supportingSentence: He moved the phone and wrote the pact above the kettle.

quiz.question: Where were the alarms supposed to stay?
options: Beside the sofa in the shared room
In the bedrooms, not in the shared room
Above the kettle with the pact
In the bathroom during every shower
quiz.correctAnswer: In the bedrooms, not in the shared room
quiz.explanation: They agreed that alarms would live in bedrooms, not in the shared room.
quiz.supportingSentence: Alarms would live in bedrooms, not in the shared room.

quiz.question: What does the following week suggest about the pact?
options: The flatmates went back to the same daily quarrel
The mornings became perfect on the first day
They took the written pact down at once
It made mornings easier without ending every slip
quiz.correctAnswer: It made mornings easier without ending every slip
quiz.explanation: The next week was not perfect, but the mornings were calmer, so the pact helped without removing every mistake.
quiz.supportingSentence: The next week was not perfect, but the mornings were calmer.

quiz.question: What does pact mean in this story?
options: A shared agreement about how the mornings will work
A broken phone alarm
A complaint about the tea
A lock on the bathroom door

quiz.explanation: The flatmates make a pact that sets who uses the shower and the kitchen first.
quiz.supportingSentence: Finally they made a simple pact.
